summary: Abandoned 1932 L-4 ground cabin in Adams County, Idaho: patrol point 1928, last staffed 1948, NHLR-registered 2020, hike-in only and reported beyond repair.

facts.status_note: Standing but abandoned since 1949; a June 2019 NHLR visit report calls it beyond repair.

access.note: On Payette National Forest land; reached only on foot with no trail to the lookout, per the NHLR 2019 visit report and Idaho Fire Lookouts' hike-in tag. Judged public because no closure or permission requirement appears in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No trail to the lookout (NHLR 2019 visit report). A 1962 USGS station description places it 5 miles north of a road end at Black Lake.

facts.agency: US Forest Service - Payette National Forest

events.note: 14 x 14 ground cabin with L-4 cab constructed (NHLR gives R1/L-4 ground cabin).
Last season the lookout was staffed (Forest Lookouts); NHLR says no longer staffed after 1948.
Abandoned, per Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com.
NHLR visit report (June 19, 2019, Wyatt Griffis): condition poor, comments say the lookout appears to be beyond repair; no trail to the lookout.
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register on September 29, 2020; nominated by Brad Eells.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says no longer staffed after 1948 and the Forest Lookouts record gives 1948 as the last staffed season; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com date abandonment to 1949. Read as one end point, not a real disagreement: last staffed 1948, abandoned 1949.
NHLR gives 8,751 ft (2,667 m); Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 8757 ft and firelookout.com gives 8747 ft. The record's 2667.3 m matches NHLR and is kept.
Idaho Fire Lookouts labels the site Abandoned and firelookout.com says it is still there. Both fit a standing but abandoned cabin, so status stays standing with a note.

notes_for_editor: Dates (1928 patrol point, 1932 cab, 1948 last staffed, 1949 abandoned, 2020 NHLR) agree across sources. Thin points: the Forest Lookouts page is an unsigned compilation, and the 2019 condition report is one visitor's report. Access 'public' is a judgement: no closure or permission found, but the site is hike-in with no trail. No notable fires were found in the sources read. Do not confuse with a Facebook post for a 1932 L-4 cab 27 miles north of Weiser, Washington County, elevation 7589 ft, which is a different tower. firelookout.com credits photos to Shawn Ogden and Luke Channer, but no URL or licence was found, so no photos are listed. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the condition findings now have evidence quotes from the NHLR form fields; the distance and the advice not to climb are sourced or marked as our judgement.
